theorem_location: MPI MiS preprint 27/2009 rev. 2010 (round-1 reading): Lemma 3.8, Lemma 3.10, Theorem 3.11, Remark 3.12, Theorem 3.18 (published numbering may differ)
verdict: Error of a product of node-wise orthogonal projections on one tensor is bounded by the root-sum-square of heterogeneous node-wise errors, in any order (Lemma 3.10); the bound depends only on the multiset of node errors (non-sharp analogue of H2); Theorem 3.18 allocates uniform node tolerances eps/sqrt(2d-3). Non-sharp (Remark 3.12), linear commuting-structure setting, no multilinear maps, no defect ratio.

theorem_location: Duplicate record (MPI MiS preprint) of 10.1137/090764189; see that row

arXiv:1407.5100v2: Prop. 2.4 (m=2, alpha=(a1+a2-2a1a2)/(1-a1a2), from Ogura-Yamada 2002 Thm 3(b)); Prop. 2.5 with phi in (2.8) (m factors, heterogeneous alpha_i, symmetric); Remark 2.7 (comparison with max-based constant (2.22))
verdict: Heterogeneous composition constant phi(alpha_1..alpha_m)=1/(1+1/sum alpha_i/(1-alpha_i)) for T_1...T_m, symmetric in the alpha_i (order-independent) and strictly better than the max-based uniform constant; tightness shown elsewhere only for m=2 (Huang-Ryu-Yin 2020 Cor. 1); not stated for m>=3 in sources read. Different functional (averagedness of nonexpansive compositions), no projections interleaved with multilinear maps; closest structural analogue of H1-vs-fallback and of H2.
